# After the main window reloads, a tear-out window's close returns its pane only at lease end

## Context

Found after #20145 merged, in a downstream dock application's multi-window tier. The arm pops a pane out, reloads the main window, then closes the popped-out window. It failed once after the downstream re-pin to `d47905526b`: the pane was not home within 45 s. A worker-side probe of the same sequence measured:

| Moment | Held admission | The vessel's recorded opener | Pane home |
|---|---|---|---|
| after the main reload | — | gone from `Neo.manager.Window` | — |
| close + 3 s | `readmit`, not connected | gone | no |
| close + 25 s | released at lease end | — | yes |

The close probe resolves to a promise without throwing; it simply has no live opener to answer for the window.

## The Problem

`NativeVesselTransaction.holdReleasedVessel` holds a released vessel's pane until the opener's handle says the window closed. The handle lives in the opener document's `Neo.Main#openWindows`, and a reload of the main window replaces that document: the handle can never answer again. So once the main window has reloaded, every close of a vessel it opened waits out the reconnect lease before the pane comes home. That is 20 s where the pane used to return at once, and in one run it was longer than 45 s.

## The Architectural Reality

- **The recording.** `NativeVesselTransaction.watchVesselHandle` records `{nativeHandleKey, ownerWindowId}` once per vessel. The opener's reload drops `ownerWindowId` from `Neo.manager.Window`, which unregisters on disconnect.
- **The hold.** `holdReleasedVessel` holds whenever a handle and an owner exist. It does not check that the handle's opener is still connected.

## The Fix

In `holdReleasedVessel`, release at once (`true`) when the handle's opener is no longer a registered window: a handle whose opener departed cannot tell a close from a reload. A reload of the vessel after a reload of its opener then sends the pane home, as before #20145. Every other case keeps its hold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A unit arm: a vessel whose opener has departed returns its pane on release at once, with no hold.
- [x] The existing #20144 arms stay green, with the opener registered as a live window.
- [x] `e2e/dashboard` stays green.

## Out of Scope

Re-establishing a handle after the opener reloads: the new opener document holds no `WindowProxy` for windows its predecessor opened.
